abstract.t: This document specifies the mandatory algorithm transition timetable that defines dates for the milestones defined in RFC6916 . The timelines for each phase of action in this document may be extended if certain criteria are not met, prior to each assigned date. Please consult the current version of this document for latest timeline dates.

note.title: Requirements Language
note.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: The Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) must accommodate transitions between public keys used by Certification Authorities (CAs). A less-common transition involves migrating to a new signature algorithm suite used by CAs and Relying Parties (RPs). The process to transition to a new, or additional algorithm, is expected to completed over a timescale of months or years. This process of transition is defined in .

This document provides a timetable for the introduction of a new algorithm suite broken up into the four phases outlined in section 4. The dates in each section of the timeline MAY be extended, but never shortened, if an upcoming date target is unable to be met. Any date changes MUST be logged in as a list of changes with associated change date.

section.title: Terminology
section.t: This document assumes that the reader is familiar with the terms and concepts describe in "Algorithm Agility Procedure for the Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI)" . For reference the following terms and conventions are provided:

After this date, all CAs MUST have reissued all their signed product sets under ALgorithm Suite B.
After this date, all RPs MUST be prepared to process signed material issued under Algorithm Suite B.
After this date, a CA MAY cease issuing signed products under Algorithm Suite A. Also, after this date, an RP MAY cease to validate signed materials issued under Algorithm Suite A.
After this date, Algorithm Suite A MUST be deprecated using the process in Section 10 of and all Algorithm Suite A TALs MUST be removed from their publication points.

section.title: Algorithm Suite
section.t: The algorithm suite transition this document defines the timetable for are listed here as Algorithm Suite A and Algorithm Suite B defined in .

list.t: The signature algorithm used in certificates, CRLs, and signed objects is RSA Public-Key Cryptography Standards (PKCS) #1 Version 1.5 (sometimes referred to as "RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5") from Section 5 of [RFC4055].

The hashing algorithm used in certificates, CRLs, and signed objects is SHA-256 [SHS]. The hashing algorithm is not identified by itself when used in certificates and CRLs, as they are combined with the digital signature algorithm (see below).

When used in the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) SignedData, the hash algorithm (in this case, the hash algorithm is sometimes called a message digest algorithm) is identified by itself. For CMS SignedData, the object identifier and parameters for SHA-256 (as defined in [RFC5754]) MUST be used when populating the digestAlgorithms and digestAlgorithm fields.
NOTE: The exception to the above hashing algorithm is the use of SHA-1 [SHS] when Certification Authorities (CAs) generate authority and subject key identifiers [RFC6487].

section.title: Timetable
section.t: The following timetable is considered to be agreed-to by the community when this document is accepted as an RFC BCP. The dates for each phase will be agreed upon by the technical contacts at each of the five Regional Internet Registries (RIRs), along with a majority of CAs issuing RPKI products.

Dates in this timetable MAY be adjusted when the community shows that an adverse effect is likely to take place without an extension. A date change requires a re-publication of this document with an update to the transation log in the appendix section. The re-publication MUST be advertised broadly to all RPs and CAs.

section.title: IANA Considerations
section.t: This memo includes no request to IANA.

section.title: Security Considerations
section.t: Algorithm transitions in RPKI should be infrequent events with wide community consensus. This document does not address algorithm security or weakness. However, an algorithm suite change addressed in the timetable defined in this document may expose CAs and RPs to a vulnerable state from maintaining and running software requiring dual-algorithm support for an extended period of time.

Any CA unable to complete its migration to the new algorithm suite by the End-Of-Life date will no longer have a signed product set validated by RPs. A CA without a validated, signed product set, will expose objects that were formerly VALID in RPKI as now UNKNOWN. These RPKI ROA objects may be targets of BGP hijacking until the CA is able to produce a signed product set using the new algorithm suite B. The community is strongly encouraged to monitor the transition process and use all possible mechanisms to ensure complete compliance with the new algorithm before the EOL date.

section.title: Timetable Change History
section.t: This section serves as a log for all timetable date changes. In an ideal situation this section will have no entries. The only time an entry is to be made to this section is when a target date cannot be met and requires a new date in the future.
